request.spec:
The consolidated figures gain, per grade on any sheet of the tree, the due-totals of the people on
that grade (retired people left out) added up over the tree, and per status the count of claims in
that status over the tree.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The consolidated figures gain, per grade on any sheet of the tree, the due-totals of the people on
that grade (retired people left out) added up over the tree, and per status the count of claims in
that status over the tree.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures now show a due-total for each grade and a claim count for each status, added up over the sheet and all the sheets below it. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

The only file I changed is `src/main/frontend/features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx`. The consolidated panel already worked out each sheet's figures in the browser, so I added the new ones in the same place and didn't need to touch the server or the stored data.

- **Per grade** (`consolidated-grade-{A,B,C}-due-total`): on each sheet, it takes the people who aren't retired, finds the grade each holds on that sheet's own today, and adds up their due-totals. Then it adds those up across the tree. A due-total of `n/a` is skipped, as in the existing summary.
- **Per status** (`consolidated-status-{DRAFT,OPEN,PENDING,SETTLED,VOID,REVIEW}-count`): it counts the claims in each status on every sheet of the tree and adds the counts together.

Both reuse code the app already had: the grade list, the rule for which grade is in force on a date, the per-person due calculation and the list of statuses. They therefore give the same numbers as the per-sheet summary, just summed over the tree.
